title_or_table: 2024 Cartographic Boundary File (SHP), 119th Congressional Districts for United States, 1:5,000,000
observation_period: Districts of the 119th Congress, seated January 2025 through December 2026 (elected November 5, 2024), as the states reported them to the Bureau by May 31, 2024
geography: The 435 districts of the 50 states (six of them at large) and the six delegate areas of DC, Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and the U.S. Virgin Islands (441 features)
universe_or_base: Congressional districts of the 119th Congress in the Bureau’s 1:5,000,000 file; boundaries only, no data values
unit: decimal degrees of longitude and latitude, NAD83
vintage: 2024 Cartographic Boundary Files (GENZ2024), posted April 10, 2025; metadata dated May 2025
qualification: Generalized for display at 1:5,000,000 or smaller and clipped to a simplified coastline, so some small areas and offshore parts are left out; not for measuring area or perimeter, geocoding addresses, or settling precise boundaries (the Bureau’s terms). A boundary file carries no data values: a map’s CSV joins on geoid or code. The kit projects and simplifies at build.

geoid.description: the Bureau’s GEOID: state FIPS code and district number, four digits

name.description: district name as the Bureau prints it (NAMELSAD), such as "Congressional District 23"

district.description: district number as the Bureau gives it, two digits; "AL" for an at-large seat (the Bureau’s 00); "98" for a delegate area, whose member has no vote on the House floor

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Cartographic Boundary Files, 2024, congressional districts of the 119th Congress, 1:5,000,000. Retrieved November 13, 2026.
coordinates: NAD83 longitude and latitude as published, unprojected and unsimplified

terms_of_use.file_metadata: Use Constraints: The intended display scale for this file is 1:5,000,000. This file should not be displayed at scales larger than 1:5,000,000. These products are free to use in a product or publication, however acknowledgement must be given to the U.S. Census Bureau as the source. The boundary information is for visual display at appropriate small scales only. Cartographic boundary files should not be used for geographic analysis including area or perimeter calculation. Files should not be used for geocoding addresses. Files should not be used for determining precise geographic area relationships.
terms_of_use.product_page: The cartographic boundary files are simplified representations of select geographic areas from the Census Bureau’s Master Address File/Topologically Integrated Geographic Encoding and Referencing (MAF/TIGER) System. These boundary files are specifically designed for small scale thematic mapping. ... For more details about these files, including their appropriate usage, please see our Cartographic Boundary File Description page.
terms_of_use.description_page: Limitations. These files should not be used for: geographic analysis including area or perimeter calculation. geocoding addresses. determining precise geographic area relationships. Some small geographic areas are excluded from these files. Geographic areas may not align with the same areas from another year.
terms_of_use.read: Read November 13, 2026: the use and access constraints in the zip’s own ISO metadata (cb_2024_us_cd119_5m.shp.iso.xml), quoted word for word; the product page (https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.2024.html) and the description page it names for appropriate usage (https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/technical-documentation/naming-convention/cartographic-boundary-file.html). notes: Converted by work/build/scripts/phase-3/research_geometry_freeze.py with its own shapefile reader (Python standard library), checked against pyshp 3.1.8 feature by feature, run with python3 -I.

Coordinates are rounded to six decimals (about 0.1 meter), as R1-C7 allows. Every vertex is kept but 8: rounding made each of those equal to the vertex before it, less than 0.1 meter away in the Bureau’s file, in 8 features (1309, 2001, 3103, 3705, 3711, 3902, 5109, 5401), and each was dropped so no segment has zero length. Neighboring districts drop the same vertex, so their shared edges stay identical.

Rings follow RFC 7946, section 3.1.6: outer rings counterclockwise, holes clockwise. That is the reverse of the shapefile’s order, so each ring’s vertices run in the reverse of the Bureau’s sequence, with no value changed. d3-geo expects the shapefile’s order and would need each ring reversed; a planar projection fills either way.

The file has no STUSPS field. code comes from the 20m states file for the 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico, and from the Bureau’s national_state2020.txt for American Samoa (60, AS), Guam (66, GU), the Northern Mariana Islands (69, MP) and the U.S. Virgin Islands (78, VI).
At-large seats read "AL" here (R1-C7) and "00" in the Clerk’s results file and the Gazetteer file; join on geoid. The 1:5,000,000 file holds no area coded ZZ.
